title: The disjointness situation (Conrad)
statement:
Consider schemes [def-pc-scheme], open immersions $i\colon U\to V$ and $j\colon V\to X$ [def-weil-open-immersion], a morphism $p\colon Z\to X$, a scheme $Y$ over $U$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] with structure map $a\colon Y\to U$, and a quasi-compact immersion $f\colon Y\to Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion] satisfying
$$
p\circ f=j\circ i\circ a.
$$
Identify $U$ and $V$ with their open images in $X$. Write $\overline Y$ for the scheme-theoretic image of $f$ in $Z$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], meaning here the closed subscheme defined by $\ker(\mathcal O_Z\to f_*\mathcal O_Y)$ (the kernel description applies since $f$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel]). Fix the following data.

1. A quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_1\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [pqf-def-coherent] with
$$
\overline{V\setminus U}\subseteq |V(\mathcal I_1)|\subseteq X\setminus U
$$
as subsets of the underlying topological space of $X$, and put $T_1=V(\mathcal I_1^2)$, using the ideal-sheaf power of [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Here $T_1$ is the square-zero thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] of $V(\mathcal I_1)$: the ideal of $V(\mathcal I_1)$ in $T_1$ is $\mathcal I_1/\mathcal I_1^2$.
2. A quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_2\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, with $T_2=V(\mathcal I_2)$ satisfying
$$
|T_2|\subseteq |T_1|\cap(X\setminus V)
$$
as sets.
3. The hypothesis that the structural morphism to $Z$ of the closed subscheme
$$
W=p^{-1}(T_1)\cap\overline Y
$$
factors through the closed subscheme $p^{-1}(T_2)\hookrightarrow Z$.

For a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal K$ on a scheme $S$, $V(\mathcal K)$ denotes the closed subscheme supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme], locally $\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)$ on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ where $\mathcal K$ corresponds to $K\subseteq A$; its ideal sheaf is $\mathcal K$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. The inverse images in clause 3 are scheme-theoretic: $p^{-1}(T_r)=Z\times_XT_r$ for $r=1,2$, and the intersection means $(Z\times_XT_1)\times_Z\overline Y$, with fibre products as in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus clause 3 asks for a morphism $W\to Z\times_XT_2$ over $Z$, rather than only an inclusion of underlying sets. The bar on $V\setminus U$ means topological closure in $X$; the bar on $Y$ means scheme-theoretic image in $Z$.

Let
$$
X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_1+\mathcal I_2}(X),\qquad q\colon X'\to X
$$
be the global blow-up [def-nagata-global-blowup] along the sum ideal sheaf (the subsheaf of $\mathcal O_X$ locally generated by sections of $\mathcal I_1$ and $\mathcal I_2$). Define, by the same fibre-product convention,
$$
Y'=Y\times_XX',\qquad Z'=Z\times_XX',\qquad
p'\colon Z'\to X',\qquad f'=f\times_X\mathrm{id}_{X'}\colon Y'\to Z',
$$
where $p'$ is the second projection, the map $Y\to X$ is $p\circ f$, and $f'$ is the induced morphism of fibre products. These data and hypotheses are the disjointness situation; no existence of choices $\mathcal I_1,\mathcal I_2$ is asserted.

split_report.summary: Definition-only split: retained all of Conrad’s hypotheses and both original definition dependencies; added the existing definitions of schemes, open/closed immersions, quasi-compactness, schemes over a base, quasi-coherence, ideal powers, first order thickenings, ideal sheaves and fibre products. Expanded scheme-theoretic inverse images and intersection, the factorization hypothesis, and the base-changed maps. No proof steps or new nodes are needed. Searched slopmaster2 and Mathlib: the disjointness theorem does not define the full bundle. Second reading makes the kernel definition of the quasi-compact scheme-theoretic image explicit, avoiding the erroneous maximality adjective in its dependency. Maintainer reading adds direct citations to the existing quasi-compact image/kernel theorem and quasi-coherent-ideal closed-subscheme construction; the mathematical data are unchanged.

blueprint_update.statement:
Consider open immersions $i\colon U\to V$ and $j\colon V\to X$, a morphism
$p\colon Z\to X$, a scheme $Y$ over $U$, and a quasi-compact immersion
$f\colon Y\to Z$ over $X$, so that the square

$$
(Y\xrightarrow{f}Z\xrightarrow{p}X)
\;=\;(Y\to U\xrightarrow{j\circ i}X)
$$

commutes; in particular $Y$ lies over $U$. Write $\overline Y$ for the scheme-theoretic image of $Y$ in $Z$
under $f$. Fix the following data.

1. A quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_1$ on $X$ with
$\overline{V\setminus U}\subseteq V(\mathcal I_1)\subseteq X\setminus U$
as sets, and $T_1=V(\mathcal I_1^2)$, a square-zero thickening of
$V(\mathcal I_1)$.
1. A quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_2$ on $X$ whose zero scheme
$T_2=V(\mathcal I_2)$ satisfies $T_2\subseteq T_1\cap(X\setminus V)$ as
sets.
1. The hypothesis that the closed subscheme
$p^{-1}(T_1)\cap\overline Y$ of $Z$ factors through the closed
subscheme $p^{-1}(T_2)$. Loosely: $p(p^{-1}(T_1)\cap\overline Y) \subseteq T_2\subseteq T_1\cap(X\setminus V)$, the first inclusion as
schemes and the second as sets.

Let $q\colon X'\to X$ be the blow-up of $X$ along $\mathcal I_1+\mathcal I_2$
and let $Y',Z',p'$ denote the base changes of $Y,Z,p$ along $q$.
